text:
maria: heads-up — staging canary hit a hard hang during a multi-node TP run, 8 nodes x TP=16. all ranks stuck during an all-reduce. timeout fired after 120s.

alex: ouch. which commit? any recent kernel selection or NCCL changes? :thinking:

maria: rolled back two days of changes but the hang repros on the canary binary. the suspected diff: batching heuristics + new kernel fallback path for fused attention.

sasha: timeline — did we change the KV cache serialization or sharding? that sometimes desyncs ranks if shape metadata is wrong.

maria: no KV serialization changes in that build. KV cache behavior looks normal in single-node. multi-node only. logs show each rank hitting `AllReduceStart` then nothing.

pranay: can you paste the minimal stack/log snippet? we should check NCCL op and whether we hit different algorithm selection across ranks.

maria: pasted below from rank0/rank3 side-by-side:

```
rank0: entering AllReduce(size=1.2GB) algo=ring, comm=nccl, tag=0x9f
rank0: nvtx push "allreduce/comm"
rank0: kernel launch: fused_attention_forward kernelA grid=...
rank0: waiting for allreduce completion... (120s timeout)
```

```
rank3: entering AllReduce(size=1.2GB) algo=tree, comm=nccl, tag=0x9f
rank3: nvtx push "allreduce/comm"
rank3: kernel launch: fused_attention_forward kernelB grid=...
rank3: no completion event for peer 0
```

alex: different NCCL algorithms (ring vs tree) across ranks would deadlock for same communicator. why would that happen? usually nccl chooses algorithm based on channel/bus/comm properties.

sasha: also note kernelA vs kernelB — kernel selection for attention differs due to sequence-length-based heuristic. maybe kernel selection changed memory/stream sync behavior, interleaving with NCCL calls.

pranay: good point — if one rank launches kernels on a non-default stream and doesn't call cudaStreamSynchronize before the collective, the collective might see different progress. check stream ids and whether we use CUDA graphs.

maria: confirmed: rank0 uses default stream, rank3 uses a dedicated compute stream (we recently added stream-per-shard optimization). that could explain different algo picks if NCCL detects different stream contexts.

zach: repro plan: (1) force same kernel selection across ranks, (2) force NCCL to use single algo via env NCCL_ALGO=RING, (3) run with NCCL_LOG_LEVEL=INFO and GPU nvprof traces.

maria: started a run with `NCCL_ALGO=RING NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` pinned to same kernel variant across ranks. will report.

infra-bot: deploy queued: canary/2026-03-18-1795000123 -> staging (image: inference-runtime:canary-1795). ETA ~2m.

deploy-bot: canary deployed to 8 nodes.

maria: early result: with NCCL_ALGO=RING the hang moved later (80s) but still occurs consistently when sequence length spikes above 1024.

alex: that suggests the problem is interaction between long-seq kernels and the collective scheduling. any kernel that uses cudaEvent synchronization or host-side waits could stall the collective progress.

pranay: can you capture per-rank stream activity and CUDA event timelines? using nsight systems or `cupti` traces. also check if we have mixed 32/16-bit kernel codepaths selected — different kernel might allocate larger temp buffers and change launch order.

sasha: also look at our batching heuristic — when batch shapes vary, we sometimes switch to a fallback kernel that does a full transpose on GPU, which adds extra kernels before the collective. if one rank switches to fallback and others don't, launch-order mismatch becomes possible.

maria: attached perf snapshot (short):
- rank0: fallback=false, kernel=attn_fast_fused, launches=3, pre-allreduce memcopy=none
- rank3: fallback=true, kernel=attn_fallback, launches=7, does a gpu->gpu memcpy and a sync event before allreduce

zach: there we go. rank3 inserts memcpy+event. if that event synchronizes host-side or different stream semantics, rank0's collective might start earlier and nccl algorithm negotiator could diverge.

alex: immediate mitigation: force unified kernel selection by disabling fallback when running multi-node TP. add a runtime guard: if world_size>1 then disallow fallback kernel. Low-risk canary.

pranay: agree. also open a perf regression ticket for the kernel-fallback path — we need to ensure it's stream-safe and doesn't insert implicit host syncs.

maria: I pushed a canary build that disables fallback under PROC_ENV=multi_node. kicking off another run.

maria: update — canary passed 50 runs without hang. pushing patch to main, but post-merge we should schedule a deeper trace: gather Nsight traces with timeline across all ranks and verify kernel/collective ordering.

sasha: follow-ups:
- add tests that run mixed-kernel scenarios across ranks in CI (small scale)
- add an assert in runtime that verifies no implicit host sync before collectives
- audit kernel selection heuristics for stream-safety

alex: also add a debug flag to force per-rank verbose kernel selection logs (include stream id, chosen grid, workspace size). that'll help when we see intermittent desyncs.

maria: filing PRs: 1) revert fallback in multi-node (canary pass) 2) add logging + assert 3) perf fix for fallback to remove host-sync. cc @sasha @pranay

pranay: thanks — once merged, let's run a long soak with variable seq lengths and batching patterns to ensure no flakiness. :eyes:

maria: agreed. will schedule soak for 24h on staging after merges. thanks everyone.
